title: openccu-lite addon manifest (openccu-lite.json)
description: What an addon declares about itself for openccu-lite: identity, texts, compatibility, where its releases are, how the shell opens it and what it needs to run. See docs/manifest-format.md.

text.description: A text in German and English, or one string for both.

id.description: The addon's rc.d id: the name its update_script links into /usr/local/etc/config/rc.d.

version.description: The package's version; informational, the installed version is read from the rc.d script's info.

summary.description: One line for the catalogue's card, at most 80 characters per language (occulited task 188). A system cuts a longer one with an ellipsis.

assets.description: architecture (uname -m) → asset pattern, for projects that do not name packages by uname -m

fallback_asset.description: tried when asset matches nothing: a package for every architecture

lite.description: the oldest openccu-lite the addon runs on

rega.description: the addon needs the ReGa, which openccu-lite does not have

icon.description: a square icon, SVG preferred, the path from the package root (the archive's root, where openccu-lite.json lies); the install keeps it from the archive

logo.description: a wide logo, the path from the package root, as icon

settings_url.description: the settings page where the addon's Config-Url is not it

session_header.description: this version reads X-Occulite-Session everywhere the shell opens it

own_updater.description: the addon still carries an update mechanism of its own

fullscreen.description: the frontend offers its own way back to the system, so the shell may show it as the whole window once the user switches that on

regadom_import_url.description: the addon's page that imports from the CCU's ReGa database kept after the switch (occulited task 168; openccu-lite from 2.0.0-rc.1): the welcome page and the Backup page link it while the database is there

capabilities.description: confined addons may not declare a root-equivalent capability (B-251); a root addon may

groups.description: confined addons may not declare occulite or root (B-251)

web_ingress.description: the addon brings connections from outside into the web server through a PROXY-protocol socket of its own and may claim client addresses inside these ranges (openccu-lite task 406)

bin.description: a directory inside the addon's tree, relative to /usr/local/addons/<id> ("bin"), made root's by the system and appended to the PATH of interactive login shells while the addon is installed and switched on (occulited task 136; openccu-lite from 1.2.1)

timers.description: the program the addon's own timers run (occulited task 154; needs runtime.bin and the scope timers:addon): the system renders each timer's service itself, with this program in the runtime.bin directory, these arguments and the timer's name as the last one

rpc_interface.description: the addon is an interface process of its own (occulited task 169; openccu-lite from 2.0.0-rc.1): it speaks the interface processes' XML-RPC on 127.0.0.1:<port><path>, and the system lists it in InterfacesList.xml under this name while the addon is installed and switched on, so lite-rpc offers it like the radios' interfaces

read_addon_data.description: a timer of this addon may name other installed addons whose data its run reads; its service then runs with those addons' own groups (occulited task 154)

to.description: makes the declaration a range from the port to this one, one switch keyed by the first port (openccu-lite task 105; occulited from openccu-lite 1.3.0 on)

backup.description: how the addon takes part in the system backup (openccu-lite task 399; occulited from openccu-lite 1.3.0 on): a hook the system runs as the addon before every backup's tar writes a consistent snapshot of the addon's data into a staging directory inside its tree, which the tar takes; paths relative to /usr/local/addons/<id>

hook.description: the program run before the tar, as the addon's user in its confinement: writes the snapshot (SQLite: VACUUM INTO) into staging; a failure or timeout is named on the Backup page and the backup goes on without it

staging.description: the directory the hook writes into; the system empties it after the tar; a restore brings the snapshot back into it; never a parent of hook or restore

timeout.description: the hook's limit in seconds (120 when absent)

size_hint_mb.description: the snapshot's expected size, shown on the Backup page; above 100 the addon's snapshot is off by default until the user switches it on

restore.description: a program the addon's unit runs before every start (ExecStartPre, as the unit's user): with a snapshot in staging after a restore it puts the data back where it lives unless the file there is newer, then empties staging; with nothing there it does nothing

targets.description: the addon provides backup targets (occulited task 150; from the first openccu-lite image after 2.0.0-beta.6): its destinations appear under Add target on the Backup page, and the system hands each encrypted backup to the addon's daemon over the Unix socket /run/occulite/backup-targets/<id>/target.sock (docs/backup-provider.md); a block with targets alone needs neither hook nor staging

label.description: the kind's word on the Backup page (the Add target button, the card), at most 40 characters per language

setup.description: the in-app path where the user makes destinations (the addon's page), linked as Connect an account…
